newsitem.title: FRANCE: Jospin - French govt does not favour privatisations.
newsitem.headline: Jospin - French govt does not favour privatisations.

text.p: Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Thursday his government did not favour privatisations of telecommunications, electronics or aerospace companies, but accepted that they needed to adapt and form partnerships with other European companies.

"In the absence of a justification based on the national interest, we are not favourable to the privatisation of this shared heritage that the big state enterprises in competitive industries represent," Jospin said in a keynote address to parliament.
"Even so, it will be necessary for them to adapt in order to retain our rank among the most developed nations of the world and to get closer to other European partners," he said.
He said the government's stance was in response to the growing debate over who should own companies in the public sector, "be they telecommunications, electronics, aerospace or other sectors".
The new Socialist-led government effectively suspended the partial privatisation of France Telecom scheduled to begin in early June.
The election also raised doubts about the privatisation of defence electronics firm Thomson-CSF launched by the previous conservative government.
